content.abstract:
Twenty Third Indian Antarctic Expedition
Ministry of Earth Sciences, Technical Publication No. 21, pp 349-359
Physiological and Ergonomic Studies at Antarctica
Abhishek Bharadwaj
Defence Institute of Physiology and Allied Sciences, Timarpur 
Delhi -  54
ABSTRACT
Physiological responses to understand effect of extreme condition, viz. sub zero 
temperature, low humidity and high wind velocity along with Ergonomic studies were 
carried out at base station, Maitri during 23r d  summer expedition 2003 -2004. Recordings 
were made on 14 volunteers from scientific and logistic groups of the expedition team 
before the start of voyage, on-board ship to Antarctica and throughout the summer months 
at Maitri (70°45’S, 11°44’E). Physiological parameters like Heart Rate, Blood Pressure, 
Hand grip strength and Pedometer studies along with Ergonomic studies and Habitability 
survey were carried out. It was observed that heart rate increased from base-line value of 75 
bpm ±0.13 to 85 bpm ± 0.21 (p<0.001), systolic blood pressure increased from 119.9 mm 
Hg ±0.15 to 128.4mm Hg ±0.53 (p<0.001) and diastolic Blood pressure increased from 
79.9 mm Hg ±0.14(SEM) to 84.3mmHg ±0.12 during the voyage (p<0.001). The rise was 
persistent till the 4th  week of stay. Heart Rate and Systolic Blood pressure showed a 
decline after the 4th  week whereas Diastolic Blood Pressure decline was not significant. The 
recordings of physiological parameters did not reach pre-voyage (base-line) levels. Energy 
consumption increased from base-line value of 219 ±0.95 kcal/hr to 297 ± 0.32 kcal/hr 
suggesting need for more energy during normal walk on Antarctic terrain as compared to 
level ground. No change was observed in Handgrip Strength of the volunteers during study. 
The over-wintering members did suggest the need of improvement for making their stay 
more comfortable at Maitri. Ergonomic study showed that immediate attention was needed 
towards electrical and flooring maintenance at the base station workshop.
INTRODUCTION
Sustaining life at polar station involves many stressful factors. 
Most of the studies carried out at different Antarctic stations have shown 
marked amount of variations in the physiological parameters of team 
members. Extensive studies have been conducted to evaluate the changes 
in body functions induced by various stress at Antarctica. Most researchers

350 Abhishek Bharadwaj
have concentrated to study the state of individual function system in response 
to these environmental and psychological stresses (Budd & Warhaft, 1966; 
Wyndhan et al., 1964; Wyndhan et al. 1968; Duncan, 1988; Buguet et al., 
1987). Subsequent studies by American, European and Australian 
researchers started exploring the performance changes as an effect of 
Antarctic exposure (Soroko et al, 1984; Palinkas 1987; Bodey, 1978). It 
was shown from studies conducted by Kruk et al and Bittel et al, that 
moderate cold may have minimal effect upon healthy individuals (Bittel et 
al, 1988; Kurk et al, 1991), whereas severe continued exposure has negative 
influence. Herr and White showed that due to extreme continuous exposure 
to cold, normal physiological balance of individuals get altered (Herr & 
White, 1991). The data available on impact of such extreme conditions 
likely extreme low temperature, high wind velocity and restricted mobility 
on physiological variables, are very limited in reference with tropical 
expedition members.
Present study was conducted on 23r d  Indian Antarctic Expedition 
Members to elucidate a) the effects of Antarctic environment on physiological 
parameters b) requirement of energy expenditure during normal walking 
on Antarctic terrain and c) Ergonomic studies at Indian Antarctic Base 
Station, Maitri (70°45’S, 11°44’E) during 2003 -  2004.
MATERIALS AND METHODS
The observations were made before commencement of journey from 
Cape Town, on-board ship and during stay at Maitri (January 2004 to March 
2004).
Subjects:  Fourteen expedition members gave consent and volunteered 
for the study. They were aged between 24years and 54 years (38.5± 1.46 
years). Their initial weight ranged from 52.48kgs to 78.56kgs (65.52± 1.49 
kgs) and height between 166cms and 182cms (174± 1.12cms). The 
volunteers were from scientific and logistic group.
a) Physiological Parameters :_Heart Rate was monitored using Polar 
Heart rate monitor (Polar electro Model No. CE 0537, Malaysia) for 24 
hours having regular intervals between readings of every subject before, 
while travelling and during stay at Maitri. Blood Pressure Monitor was 
monitored using Oscillation Method based Blood Pressure Monitor (Make: 
Omron CH 606, USA). Hand grip Dynamometer (Jammer, USA) was used 
to measure hand grip strength of each volunteers during travel and throughout 
the summer months at Antarctica.
